This is an appeal filed by the appellant/accused aggrieved against the judgment passed by XXXIII ACMM, Bengaluru, in CC No.58175/2017 on 28.12.2022 convicting the appellant for the offence punishable u/S 138 of N.I. Act and sentencing him to pay a fine of Rs.31,05,000/- and in default to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 6 months.
2. The appellant was the accused and respondent herein was the complainant before the trial court and hereinafter they are referred to as per the ranks assigned to them before the trial court.

3. In brief the appellant/accused has stated in the memorandum of appeal that the trial court has convicted him in C.C. No.58175/2017 for the offence punishable u/S 138 of N.I. Act by holding that he has issued the cheque bearing No.692153, dated 25.05.2017 for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/-
CRL.A. No.25020/2023 in favour of the complainant.

The said judgment has been challenged by the accused on the following grounds:-
1. That the impugned order passed by the trial court is contrary to law, facts,
probabilities & circumstances of the case.

2. That the trail court failed to note that, the disputed cheque is not a valid cheque as per Sections 4 & 6 of N.I. Act, despite the accused denied the issuance of cheque and signatures appears on the cheque, erroneously convicted the accused.

The accused issued reply notice and took plea that the disputed cheque and another cheque has been misplaced in the month of February, 2017, immediately he lodged a police complaint on 16.02.2017, apart from that, the accused gave representation to the bank for stop payment, the complaint is a relative of the accused and he might have stolen the disputed cheque, got dishonoured in order to owe wrongful gain.

sentences.text: That the transaction if any took place between the father of the accused and deceased complainant, the accused CRL.A. No.25020/2023 cannot be held liable,
since the accused is not a party to the special power of attorney and the agreement of sale and therefore at any stretch of imagination, the accused cannot be convicted by the trial court.
4. That the PW-1 produced Ex.P.8 SPA and Ex.P.9 agreement of sale, which are unregistered documents both dated 15.02.2010.

The time was fixed for 6 months from 15.02.2010 to 2017 nearly 7 years and above, the complainant had not taken any action either by issuing the legal notice, in action on the part of PW-1 nearly 7 years and above, inspires the confidence of the court that the case set up by the complainant is false and frivolous.
5. That the complainant claiming to be tendered Rs.20.00 lakhs to the father of accused, the same is unaccounted transactions, since the said amount had not been disclosed in the Income Tax Returns.
6. That the P.W.1 categorically admits that there is no agreement between P.W.1 and the accused to show that the accused agreed to repay the amount of CRL.A.
No.25020/2023 Rs.20.00 lakhs given to his father by adding Rs.10.00 lakhs.

Admittedly, provisions of Section 269SS of the Income Tax Act has not been followed, as it is not the case of the complainant that Rs.30.00 lakhs tendered by means of account payee cheque and therefore the accused is required to be acquitted.

7. That the evidence on record is clear that the complainant does not establishes any legal debt and liability on the part of the accused and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.
No settlement between the complainant and the accused has been taken place, accordingly question of issuing the Ex.P.1 does not arise at all.
Towards the alleged settlement, no witnesses have been examined.
Thereby on all these grounds the appellant has prayed for setting aside the judgment dated 28.12.2022 passed by XXXIII ACMM Court.
4. After filing of this appeal, the presence of the respondent was secured.
The trial court record was called and received.
Heard arguments.
The counsel for complainant has submitted written submissions and perused the entire materials placed on record.

10. In brief it is the case of the complainant before the trial court that the accused is his relative,
based on that acquaintance, father of the accused during lifetime, for the benefit of family necessities had executed agreement of sale with General Power of Attorney in his favour on 15.02.2020 with respect to land bearing Sy.No.1, measuring 4 Acres situated Arebannimangala Village, Devanahalli Taluk by receiving an advance sale consideration amount of Rs.20 CRL.A.
No.25020/2023 lakhs through cheque bearing No.679708, dated 15.02.2010 drawn on Kaveri Grameena Bank Mallinathapura Branch.

However, after entering into an agreement of sale, the KIADB acquired property subjected under agreement of sale, by knowing the same, the complainant claims to have demanded the accused as well as the father of the accused for refund of advance amount.

But the accused promised him to repay it along with interest as soon as KIADB releases compensation to the accused and his father, believing the same, he waited for some time, but in the meantime, the father of the accused Narayanappa had died in the 2nd week of September 2015,
however, after death of accused father, he claimed to have intimated the accused to file objection along with the agreement as well as GPA executed by the father of the accused to KIADB, but the accused promised him again to refund the advance amount along with the interest within six months, considering the relationship and to have good relationship with the relatives, CRL.A.
No.25020/2023 he granted further one more year, however, even after completion of one year accused failed to pay advance amount, but in the last week of April 2017, on his demand the accused issued cheque bearing No.692153, dated 25.05.2017 drawn on Vijaya Bank, Mylanahalli Branch in his favour with an assurance that, cheque would be honoured as the KIADB authorities will release the amount in the third week of May 2017, accordingly, he claims to have presented cheque on 01.06.2017 for encashment, but the said cheque was returned with an endorsement 'Payment Stopped by Drawer' dated 12.06.2017.
Thereby the complainant got issued a notice to the accused on 16.06.2017.
The said notice was served upon the accused on 19.06.2017.
In spite of it, the accused failed to pay the amount.

Thereby he filed the complaint against the accused on 11.07.2017 for the offence punishable u/S 138 of N.I. Act.
CRL.A. No.25020/2023 11.
The trial court records would show that after filing of this complaint the court has taken the cognizance of the offence and has recorded the sworn statement, registered the case against the accused.

Further the records would also show that after the presence of the accused has been secured, substance of accusation has been recorded, the accused has not pleaded guilt and thereafter the trial court has recorded the evidence of the complainant and the accused, on the basis of the Santosh vs B Gopal, Rep. 13. The main ground of the accused in preferring this appeal is that during the cross-examination of P.W.1, the complainant has admitted that the annual income from the agriculture is about 4 to 5 lakhs and he has not shown the said amount in his agricultural income.

Further P.W.1 has deposed at page-3 of his cross-examination is as follows:-
'I know the contents of sale agreement Ex.P.9 and GPA Ex.P.8.
I do not know that the property stated in sale agreement Ex.P.9 and power of attorney Ex.P.8 has been notified for preliminary acquisition.
I do not know that there were final notification on 29.09.2008 in respect of aforesaid properties stated in Ex.P.8 and P.9 for acquisition.

I do not know that on 14th and 15th July 2009 by preparing JMC sketch,
the KIADB has taken the possession of property stated in Ex.P.8 and P.9.' CRL.A.
No.25020/2023
Further P.W.1 has deposed at page-7 of his cross- examination is as follows:-
'I do not know that after the death of Narayanappa entire family has been looked after by one Ravi who is the son of Narayanappa through 1st wife.

When it is questioned to the witness that you have advanced Rs.20 lakhs to the father of the accused and your claiming that the accused has issued cheque for Rs.30 lakhs and as such how you have calculated Rs.10 lakhs; the witness said that the accused,
his brother Ravi came near his house and told me that they will add Rs.10 lakhs and agreed to pay Rs.30 lakhs in the presence of conciliators and issued the cheque.'
Further P.W.1 has deposed at page-8 of his cross- examination is as follows:-
'It is false to suggest that in spite of the knowledge of acquisition of property by KIADB I have entered into a sale agreement with the accused.
It is true that there is no agreement in the family of accused that on CRL.A. No.25020/2023 behalf of other members the accused alone will pay the amount due to me...............................
I know the contents of reply notice issued by the accused.
I do not know that the Ex.P.1 (a) signature is not the signature of accused.

I do not know that the ink used to put the signature is different from the other writings in the cheque.'

During the cross-examination of P.W.4, she has admitted that after knowing the fact of acquisition of land by KIADB there was no written document has been executed between her husband and the accused or his father or family members of the accused in respect of the property stated in sale agreement and there is no written agreement between complainant and the accused that they have received money from her husband and agreed to repay the amount to her husband.

Further she has admitted that there is no reference of execution of agreement and GPA by the father of the accused in Ex.P.13 (a), which does not discloses that the payment of Rs.20 lakhs by her husband or the accused agreed to repay the said amount by adding Rs.10 lakhs to it.

16. The other ground on which the accused has challenged the appeal is the complainant utterly fails to prove his case beyond the reasonable doubt, that the CRL.A. No.25020/2023 accused is legally due any amount to the complainant and without considering the material on record has wrongly convicted the accused.

17. The evidence given by D.W.1 before the court, that is, the accused, would show that he being the relative used to visit his house often and taken away their cheques and the signature found in the Santosh vs B Gopal, Rep.

During the course of cross-examination of D.W.1, he has admitted that the property in Sy.No.1 measuring 4 Acres of Arebinnamangala is the self acquired property of his father and along with this property their another property in Sy.No.6/4 measuring 1 Acre 21 Guntas have been acquired by KIADB.

Further at page-5 of his cross-examination he has deposed as follows:-
'It is false to suggest that the property in Sy.No.1 was standing the name of my father C.Narayanappa till the year 2013-14 as per M.R. H8/2012-13.
It is false to suggest that my father by giving all these CRL.A. No.25020/2023 documents entered into an agreement with the complainant.'
Further D.W.1 has admitted that he has received the notice issued by the complainant and he had given a reply.

Further he deposed in the month of February 2017 he has lost the cheque but he do not remember the exact date in which he has lost the cheque and in Ex.D.4 the name of the complainant has been mentioned as Sampath Kumar.A.N.

The evidence given by D.W.2 before the court, that is, the Senior Branch Manager, Bank of Baroda,
Mylanahalli Branch, would show that the accused is customer of their bank and he has admitted that the signature of the accused found on PAN card and Ex.P.1 are different.
18.
Except denial accused has not made any venture to raise any probable defence.

Merely because,
the complainant in his evidence state that he has not shown the amount in his income tax return, it cannot be said that complainant has not paid the amount to the accused.

It is CRL.A.
No.25020/2023 not the case of the accused that the accused was not having financial capacity.

If the entire cross-examination directed to the complainant by accused is carefully perused, it would show that except suggestions nothing has been elicited to raise suspicion or to shift burden on the complainant to prove his case.

It is well settled principle of law that when the accused has failed to substantiate or raise any probable defence through which the burden can be shifted, it has to be hold that the accused has committed an offence u/S 138 of N.I. Act.
19.
Here in this case cheque came to be dishonoured on the ground of payment stopped by the drawer.
But, the accused taken a defence that signature is different.
So defence taken by the accused is not sustainable and more over the accused taken another defence that the debt is time barred debt.
To prove with respect to the time barred debt the sale as well as GPA here in this case the claimed liability CRL.A. No.25020/2023 is not time barred.
Admittedly KIADB release the amount in the year 2017 after accused issued Ex.P.1 cheque towards the amount of advance consideration amount within 3 years from the date of revocation of the GPA.
So, merely taken defence material alteration of the disputed cheque and legally debt and the liability and adverse inference are required to be proved by the accused.
But, here in this case perusal of the material available on record the accused failed to prove the defences taken by him.

Here in this case P.W.2 is attesting witness of the sale, P.W.3 is sister of the accused supports the case of the complainant and more over Ex.P.11 shows that as on 16.02.2010 the bank balance of the complainant is Rs.33,65,480/-.
It shows that the complainant is having financial capacity.

However, accused though denied the cheque as well as signature found on the cheque, but admitted Ex.P.1 Cheque is belonged to him and Santosh vs B Gopal, Rep. By Lrs on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129537686/

He is having sufficient balance in his account.
So, the contention taken by the accused clearly goes to show all the defence of the accused after thought one only to escape from the liability.

Here in this case sister of the complainant examined and she deposed that her brother accused agreed to refund Rs.20,00,000/- with interest and agreed to pay Rs.30,00,000/- for delayed payment and from the record goes to show that on 15.02.2010 a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- received from the father of the accused.
The evidence of P.W.3 on record shows settlement held between accused and complainant for Rs.30,00,000/-, so in this regard Ex.P.1 is executed.
So Ex.P.1 Cheque is legally enforceable debt.
Therefore accused failed to establish probable defence that cheque had been stolen by the complainant and signature found on the cheque is not belonged to the accused.

The trial court by considering the entire materials on record has rightly come to the conclusion that the accused has failed to rebut the presumption, which lies in favour of the complainant and more over recently the Hon'ble Apex Court in Crl.Appeal at Special Leave Petition (Crl.)
No.12802/2022, dated 09.10.2023 between Rajesh Jain v/s Ajay Singh

sentences.text: has in detail discussed as to how the presumption operates and once the presumption operates, the onus rests on the accused to prove the non-existence of debt/liability.
Wherein in the said above referred case, the accused was tried for the offence u/S 138 of N.I. Act.

The trial court had acquitted the accused by considering that the onus of rebutting the presumption lay on the accused was discharged by raising a probable defence and the complainant has failed to prove his case beyond reasonable doubt and the defence of the accused has created a doubt regarding the truthfulness of the complainant case.
Against the order of acquittal passed by the trial court, the CRL.A. No.25020/2023 complainant had preferred the appeal before the Hon'ble High Court.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court also upheld the order of acquittal holding that the complainant has failed to prove that the cheque was issued in respect of legally enforceable debt.

Wherein in the said case, it was the defence taken by the accused that the complainant had failed to mention the date, month and the year on which he advanced various sum of money towards the loan to the accused.

The version of the complainant was doubtful, since the cheque was admittedly issued in part payment of outstanding dues and no where in the complaint or demand notice complainant disclosed the total amount loan to the accused.

The court found that the complainant therein was an Orthopedic Surgeon could not have advance huge amount to an accused who was a Class-IV employee without an agreement or acknowledgement of loan advance etc.

When the matter went up to Hon'ble Apex Court, the Hon'ble Apex Court in detail have discussed as to when a presumption is CRL.A. No.25020/2023 raised, how the accused have to rebut the said presumption and when the burden shifts on the complainant and at para- 56, page-33 the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed;
'56.

At the stage when the courts concluded that the signature had been admitted, the Court ought to have inquired into either of the two questions (depending on the method in which accused has chosen to rebut the presumption): Has the accused led any defense evidence to prove and conclusively establish that there existed no debt/liability at the time of issuance of cheque?
In the absence of rebuttal evidence being led the inquiry would entail: Has the accused proved the Santosh vs B Gopal, Rep.

9 nonexistence of debt/liability by a preponderance of probabilities by referring to the 'particular circumstances of the case'?'
21.

Further Hon'ble Apex Court has clearly held as to when the presumption is rebutted and when the court has to shift the burden on the complainant to prove the case and what are all the facts,
which can be considered as rebuttal evidence.

In the background of the discussion held by the Hon'ble Apex Court, if the facts and circumstances as well as CRL.A. No.25020/2023 the evidence led by the parties are perused carefully, they would show that the accused though had led the evidence, but the evidence is not satisfactory to say that there is a probability in his defence and to shift the burden on the complainant to prove the transaction.
I have perused the above rulings of the advocate for the appellant.

The above rulings of the advocate for the appellant not applicable to the present case in hand and the facts and circumstances of above ruling are entirely different and defences taken by the accused cannot be acceptable at all.
When such being the fact, I hold there is nothing on record to interfere in the judgment passed by the trial court.

Accordingly, I hold point for consideration No.1 in Affirmative and No.2 in Negative and proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.
